transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Evan Hart (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE); Raj Patel (CascadeFin Head of ML), Sofia Alvarez (Platform Lead), Tom Li (CISO), Grace Kim (SRE)

Summary:
CascadeFin is evaluating Redwood Dedicated to run production LLM inference for customer-facing features (document summarization, extraction, and chat). They are leaning toward Dedicated because of strict isolation/data policies and predictable cost, but want clarity on burst handling, autoscaling behavior, reserved GPU sizing, and security/compliance integration (KMS, SSO, audit logs). They asked for a pilot/benchmark and detailed pricing. Next steps captured at end.

Topics: reserved GPUs, burst capacity / autoscale, model variants, latency SLOs, KV/prefix caching, quantization, security (SOC2/KMS/SSO), rollout/canary testing, observability

Transcript:
[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro - I'm Evan, AE, with Priya and Marco from the SE team. Raj, Sofia, Tom, Grace, thanks for making time. Can I confirm we're about 45 minutes?
[00:12] Raj: Yep that works. We're trying to decide between Redwood Hosted and Dedicated. Primary drivers are isolation and cost predictability - we have regulated data and our security team wants no co-tenancy.
[00:25] Priya: Got it. Can you share a bit about your expected QPS, typical request latency targets, and models you plan to run? Even ballpark numbers help.
[00:35] Sofia: Sure. For phase 1 we expect 120-150 requests per minute at peak - a mix of short chat completions and longer summarization that can go to 1,000 tokens. Target p95 latency is <450ms for the chat path; summarization can be higher, ~1.2s p95.
[00:58] Grace: Also need strong audit logs and KMS integration. CISO will want SAML SSO, RBAC, and proof of data-at-rest encryption keys we manage.
[01:08] Marco: Perfect - that aligns with many Dedicated customers. For sizing reserved GPUs we look at token throughput per GPU for the model family; do you have a preferred model or are you open to recommendations?
[01:22] Raj: We're using an open Llama-variant family internally; we care about accuracy so we'll probably run a 13B-ish model quantized to 4-bit. We might try a smaller 7B for cost-sensitive paths.
[01:35] Priya: Good, quantized 13B is common. With Dedicated we recommend sizing for your steady-state and then plan burst capacity. Two options: reserved pool sized for baseline with burst instances (reserved or on-demand) for peaks, or larger reserved pool and autoscale policies. What's your tolerance for pre-warm latency during spikes?
[02:00] Sofia: We can't tolerate >1s cold starts on chat. So warm capacity for chat must be maintained. Summaries can be batched and tolerates some higher latency.
[02:10] Priya: Then we suggest reserving a warm pool for the chat route to keep KV caches hot, and a separate pool for batch jobs that uses autoscaling. For example, reserve N GPUs to cover the chat p95, and have a burst policy that adds M GPUs when queueing grows. Bursts can be instant if the infra is idle but depending on provider there may be a 30-120s spin-up.
[02:35] Tom: How does Redwood handle burst if we need immediate capacity? Is there pre-warm or instant bursting?
[02:42] Marco: Two levers - warm reserved nodes and burst buckets. For Dedicated in our hosted infra we can commit a small set of warm nodes kept online; that avoids cold-start. For larger spikes we can have capacity in a burst pool that can be activated. If you use Dedicated on your VPC/on-prem, spin-up time depends on your infra, but we can run standby instances too. We'll document expected times in the sizing sheet.
[03:00] Raj: What about model variants and fallbacks? If a high-cost model saturates, can requests fallback to a cheaper 7B automatically?
[03:08] Priya: Yes - our smart routing can fall back by policy (latency, cost) to compatible model variants. You can configure per-endpoint rollouts. We also support canary and A/B to validate quality.
[03:22] Grace: On security: can you confirm KMS options and whether we can use our HSM? Also, audit logs retention options?
[03:30] Marco: We integrate with customer-managed KMS and can support HSM-backed keys for on-prem Dedicated. Audit logs are exportable to your SIEM and retention can be configured - we have enterprise plans for longer retention. We'll attach SOC 2 and architecture docs.
[03:47] Tom: Any PCI/fin-reg stuff we should know? Our compliance team will read the docs closely.
[03:52] Evan: We'll share the security packet. Most customers in finance opt for Private (VPC) or on-prem Dedicated to meet strict controls. For many, Dedicated with customer-managed KMS and VPC peering is sufficient.
[04:06] Raj: Cost - how do you recommend we set committed capacity vs on-demand? We want predictable monthly burn but not to overcommit.
[04:15] Priya: Common pattern: commit to baseline that covers 60-80% steady usage, then allow burst/overage in on-demand with clear unit prices. We also provide recommendations on batching, prefix caching, and token limits to reduce per-token cost. We'll include model-specific throughput estimations in the sizing spreadsheet.
[04:34] Sofia: Do you support model quantization and the tradeoffs? We want the 4-bit path but need regression checks.
[04:40] Marco: Yes we support quantized models; we provide recommended quant configs and run quality monitoring. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles per workload, and you can tie regressions into evals.
[04:52] Raj: For the pilot, we'd like a benchmark that mirrors our peak 2-hour window. Can you run that against a Dedicated pilot?
[04:58] Priya: Absolutely. Typical pilot: 2-4 week trial where we provide a small reserved pool and run your traffic samples, measure latency/cost, and tune batching/caching. We'll propose a scope in the sizing doc.
[05:12] Grace: Observability - can we get token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency?
[05:17] Marco: Yes, Redwood Console shows per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost, and tracing hooks. We'll share screenshots and demo access during the pilot.
[05:28] Raj: Anything else around network / egress? We need to keep traffic within our region.
[05:33] Evan: We support regional deployments and can pin instances to regions. For Private/on-prem deployments, no egress leaves your VPC unless you opt-in for Redwood-managed services.
[05:45] Tom: SLA? We need 99.9% availability for Dedicated endpoints.
[05:50] Priya: Dedicated comes with SLA tiers. We'll map your needs to a Bronze/Silver/Gold SLA in the proposal.
[05:57] Sofia: Perfect. Let's recap next steps.
[06:00] Evan: Recap - Redwood will send: 1) dedicated sizing + pricing spreadsheet, 2) SOC2/KMS/security docs, 3) proposed pilot scope and dates. CascadeFin will provide: traffic profile and top prompts. We'll schedule the 2-hour benchmark kickoff week of 2026-03-16.
[06:19] Raj: Sounds good. One last small thing, when you say "KV cache" sometimes your transcripts say "K-V cash" which confuses folks - minor transcription note.
[06:27] Priya: Noted, thanks. We'll email links.
[06:30] Evan: Great - thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the attachments and proposed dates.
[06:35] Tom: Thanks all.
[06:37] (call ends)
